thread.title: Apple: Smartphone Market Share Creeps Upward in Q1

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Apple: Smartphone Market Share Creeps Upward in Q1
text:
Photo: Getty Images Updated May 2, 2018 10:48 a.m. ET Apple and other manufacturers saw their smartphone market share rise in the first quarter as market leader Samsung’s held fast, according to new data.
Barron’s Next 50 stock Apple (AAPL), which reported fiscal Q2 financial results on Tuesday, saw Q1 smartphone shipments finish at 52.2 million, according to IDC , up from 50.8 million in last year’s quarter. Its market share, at 15.5%, was up from 2.8% a year before. (Barron’s Tiernan Ray covered the earnings report , while Jon Swartz offered perspective on tech earnings .)
Newsletter Sign-up That happened as Samsung’s shipments fell to 78.2 million from 80.1 million and its market share held at 23.3%, according to IDC. Samsung was last year’s leader in smartphone shipments.
Global smartphone shipments fell 2.9% for the quarter to just over 334.3 million. The launch of new flagship phones bolstered results. Shipments in China, which fell below 100 million for the first time since 2013, were a major reason for the decline.
“Consumers looked unwilling to shell out big money for the latest and greatest devices on the market,” IDC’s Anthony Scarsella said in a statement.
Xiaomi saw shipments jump more than 86% to 27.6 million, while Huawei’s rose 13.8% to 11.7 million. IDC credited strong non-China growth in the latter case, while European growth was a major reason for Xiaomi’s performance.
Illustration: IDC “More affordable premium devices might be the solution the market needs in the second half of the year to drive shipments back in a positive direction,” Scarsella said.
This item was updated shortly after publication to reflect updated data distributed by IDC.
